patterns.title: Boolean Masking and Projection
patterns.short_description: Filters DataFrame rows using vectorized boolean conditions (&, |, ~) and selects specific column subsets or views.
mental_triggers: Select rows where age > 25 and status is active
Filter dataframe based on multiple column constraints
Subset specific columns from a large dataframe
constraint_signals: Vectorized boolean indexing avoids Python row-by-row iteration; bitwise operators &, | require parentheses around conditions
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N * C) vectorized evaluation | Space: O(M * C) filtered view/copy

patterns.title: DataFrame Merge and Join Operations
patterns.short_description: Combines two DataFrames along column keys using inner, left, right, or outer relational join semantics (pd.merge).
mental_triggers: Combine customer profiles with transaction history
Join lookup table attributes to fact records
Left join to preserve master record list with optional child data
constraint_signals: Hash join on merge keys in memory; non-unique keys produce Cartesian product on matching values
patterns.complexity: Time: O(M + N) average hash join | Space: O(M + N) merged dataframe

patterns.title: GroupBy Aggregation and Transformation
patterns.short_description: Applies split-apply-combine operations to aggregate, transform, or filter grouped records (.groupby().agg()).
mental_triggers: Calculate total and average spend per user
Find highest earner within each department
Apply custom multiple aggregation functions across different columns
constraint_signals: Split-apply-combine partitions indices; as_index=False avoids resetting index afterwards
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N) hash grouping + O(K) aggregation | Space: O(K) aggregated dataframe

patterns.title: Ranking and Row Shifting (rank and shift)
patterns.short_description: Computes dense or fractional ranks and accesses adjacent rows along an index or partition using .rank() and .shift().
mental_triggers: Find 2nd highest salary using rank(method='dense')
Compare consecutive days of stock prices using .shift(1)
Calculate lag differences between consecutive timestamp events
constraint_signals: Sorting before shifting ensures correct chronological or ordinal comparisons
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N log N) sorting + O(N) shifting | Space: O(N) series
patterns.base_template_py:
import pandas as pd

def rank_and_shift(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df["rank"] = df["score"].rank(method="dense", ascending=False)
    df["prev_score"] = df["score"].shift(1)
    return df

patterns.title: Reshaping, Pivoting, and Melting
patterns.short_description: Reorganizes DataFrame layouts between wide and long representations using pivot(), pivot_table(), and melt().
mental_triggers: Convert long transactional records into wide multi-month summary table
Unpivot wide monthly columns into standardized date/value rows
Cross-tabulate two categorical columns with aggregated values
constraint_signals: pivot() requires unique index/column pairs; pivot_table() supports aggregation for duplicate pairs
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N) reshaping | Space: O(N) restructured dataframe

patterns.title: Handling Missing Values and Deduplication
patterns.short_description: Identifies, replaces, or drops missing (NaN / None) values and removes duplicate records based on primary key subsets.
mental_triggers: Drop rows missing critical identifier columns
Fill missing scores with zero or category mean
Remove duplicate user events keeping the first or last occurrence
constraint_signals: dropna() and drop_duplicates() with subset parameter provide in-place or copy deduplication
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N) linear scan / hashing | Space: O(N) cleaned dataframe

patterns.title: Vectorized String and Datetime Operations
patterns.short_description: Performs element-wise text manipulation via .str accessor and date/time decomposition and arithmetic via .dt accessor.
mental_triggers: Filter emails matching regex pattern with .str.match()
Extract year and month from timestamp column via .dt.year
Convert string timestamps to datetime objects with pd.to_datetime
constraint_signals: Vectorized .str and .dt accessors avoid slow Python loop execution over Series elements
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N * L) string operations / O(N) date conversions | Space: O(N) series
patterns.base_template_py:
import pandas as pd

def string_datetime(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df["clean_email"] = df["email"].str.strip().str.lower()
    df["year"] = pd.to_datetime(df["created_at"]).dt.year
    return df

patterns.title: Vectorized Conditionals and Custom Mapping
patterns.short_description: Evaluates branching conditionals using np.select() / np.where() and applies custom transformations across rows or series.
mental_triggers: Categorize numeric scores into low, medium, and high bands
Compute custom row-level conditional calculations based on multiple column flags
Avoid row-by-row iteration in favor of array-level vectorization
constraint_signals: np.select() executes in compiled C array speed; .apply(axis=1) is slow fallback for complex non-vectorizable logic
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N) vectorized array evaluation | Space: O(N) output series
patterns.base_template_py:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def transform_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df["bonus"] = df["salary"] * 2
    df["tier"] = np.where(df["salary"] >= 100000, "High", "Standard")
    return df

patterns.title: DataFrame Fundamentals, Shape & Projection
patterns.short_description: Creating DataFrames from dictionaries/lists, inspecting shape and data types, renaming columns, and selecting subsets.
mental_triggers: Create a DataFrame from List: pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['col1', 'col2'])
Get the Size of a DataFrame: [df.shape[0], df.shape[1]]
Rename Columns: df.rename(columns={'old': 'new'})
Display the First Three Rows: df.head(3)
constraint_signals: Basic table instantiation and schema inspection with zero row-by-row iteration
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N * C) where C is column count | Space: O(N * C)

patterns.title: Concatenation, Sorting & Extremum Selection
patterns.short_description: Combining DataFrames along vertical axes with pd.concat, sorting rows by multiple columns, and extracting top N records.
mental_triggers: Concatenate Two DataFrames: pd.concat([df1, df2], axis=0)
Sort Rows by Column: df.sort_values(by='salary', ascending=False)
Find Top N Largest: df.nlargest(N, 'score') or df.head(N)
constraint_signals: Vertical concatenation requires aligned column headers; sort_values uses introsort O(N log N)
patterns.complexity: Time: O(N log N) for sorting | Space: O(N)

hints.title: Tabular Structure Construction
hints.text: Raw nested collections lack named axes and schema definitions. How can a two-dimensional collection of values be converted directly into an indexed tabular structure with explicit column titles?

hints.title: DataFrame Constructor Projection
hints.text: The standard DataFrame constructor accepts nested lists alongside an explicit list of column names, establishing the two-dimensional tabular representation immediately.

hints.title: Constructor Invocation with Column Names
hints.text: Call pd.DataFrame passing student_data as the first argument and columns=['student_id', 'age'] as the second argument. Return the resulting DataFrame object.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Vectorized DataFrame instantiation from 2D sequence with column naming.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating element-by-element with Python loops or appending row-by-row (df.append / concat) incurs repeated memory reallocations, creating O(N^2) quadratic copying overhead instead of contiguous array initialization.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bulk construction directly from a 2D sequence allocates contiguous memory blocks for column series in a single vectorized O(N) pass, using O(N) auxiliary memory for DataFrame internal representation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Specifying column labels directly via the columns parameter during instantiation rather than post-hoc assignment; ensuring correct integer dtype inference.

solutions.approach: Direct pd.DataFrame Constructor with Column Names

hints.title: Deriving a New Column from Existing Attributes
hints.text: Employee compensation is stored in a salary attribute. How can you calculate a doubled compensation amount for every row and attach the result as a new column labeled bonus?

hints.title: Vectorized Arithmetic Assignment Invariant
hints.text: Arithmetic operations on pandas Series operate element-wise in C without Python loop overhead, allowing direct assignment to new column names.

hints.title: Vectorized Column Creation Procedure
hints.text: Assign a new bonus column on the DataFrame set to the salary column multiplied by two. Return the updated DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import pandas as pd

def createBonusColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['bonus'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees
```

complexity.notes: Vectorized column multiplication and assignment in contiguous memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using apply() with a lambda or iterating with a loop introduces heavy interpreter overhead compared to vectorized Series arithmetic.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct vectorized column assignment scales linearly in O(N) time and allocates an O(N) Series.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using vectorized multiplication rather than apply(lambda x: x * 2).

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def createBonusColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['bonus'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees

hints.title: Selective Column Deduplication
hints.text: Multiple rows may share identical values in a specific attribute while differing across others. How can redundant records be removed based on a single chosen attribute while retaining initial occurrences?

hints.title: Subset Deduplication Method
hints.text: Pandas provides dedicated deduplication routines that allow specifying a subset of columns to evaluate, retaining the first occurrence by default.

hints.title: Targeted Column Deduplication
hints.text: Invoke drop_duplicates on the customers DataFrame, specifying subset=['email'] as an argument. Return the deduplicated DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass C-level hash table deduplication on designated subset column.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating over rows with .iterrows() and checking membership in a manual Python set takes O(N) high-overhead bytecode operations and creates temporary Series objects per row, wasting orders of magnitude more runtime than vectorized hashing.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Vectorized deduplication uses an internal C-level hash table on the designated subset column in O(N) time with O(N) memory, avoiding python object boxing.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using the subset parameter to restrict hashing to the target column; knowing default keep='first' retains the first occurrence.

hints.title: Null Value Imputation
hints.text: Certain inventory records have missing numerical quantities represented as null. How can you substitute missing values in a specific attribute with zero while keeping all other values unchanged?

hints.title: Null Imputation Invariant
hints.text: Imputing missing values with a designated default preserves the total row count and replaces null tokens without mutating valid non-null entries.

hints.title: Fillna Application Procedure
hints.text: Invoke the fillna method on the quantity Series passing zero as the replacement argument. Reassign the result to the quantity column and return the DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import pandas as pd

def fillMissingValues(products: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    products['quantity'] = products['quantity'].fillna(0)
    return products
```

complexity.notes: Single pass vectorized null imputation on targeted Series.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Manual iteration checking for NaN values is slow and prone to type mismatch errors with floating point NaN representations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Series.fillna(0) scans contiguous column memory in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Targeting only the specified column rather than calling fillna on the entire DataFrame.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def fillMissingValues(products: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    products['quantity'] = products['quantity'].fillna(0)
    return products
solutions.approach: Series Null Value Imputation with fillna

hints.title: In-Place Column Value Transformation
hints.text: Existing employee salary values need to be updated to twice their current magnitude. How can you modify the column values directly using vectorized calculations?

hints.title: Column Overwrite Invariant
hints.text: Assigning a transformed Series back to an existing column key overwrites the data in-place without altering the remaining table structure.

hints.title: Vectorized Overwrite Procedure
hints.text: Multiply the salary column Series by two and reassign the result to the salary column of the employees DataFrame. Return the modified DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import pandas as pd

def modifySalaryColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['salary'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating over rows to update values individually triggers chained indexing warnings and degrades execution speed.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place column multiplication executes in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary memory beyond the overwritten column.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Reassigning directly to df[col] with vectorized multiplication; avoiding chained assignment.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def modifySalaryColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['salary'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees

hints.title: Dimensional Orientation Shift
hints.text: Data recorded in narrow long format spreads observations across separate rows. How can distinct categorical values be rotated so that one attribute defines the row index while another forms column titles?

hints.title: Pivot Reshaping
hints.text: Pivoting reorganizes a tabular dataset by transforming unique values of a specified column into new column headers, indexed by another column and populated with a chosen value column.

hints.title: Pivot Parameter Configuration
hints.text: Call the pivot method on the weather DataFrame with index='month', columns='city', and values='temperature'. Return the transformed DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Vectorized 2D cross-tabulation pivot on unique index-column pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Manual grouping, nested dictionary accumulation, and manual matrix reshaping takes quadratic interpretation time and fails when duplicate (index, column) pairs exist. Iterating through DataFrame rows is notoriously slow.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The vectorized .pivot() engine constructs a 2D index-by-column cross-tabulation in O(N) time with O(U * V) auxiliary memory where U and V are the unique counts of index and column values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Selecting .pivot() when index-column combinations are unique; naming index, columns, and values kwargs accurately.

hints.title: Targeted Record Column Selection
hints.text: A student roster stores multiple attributes across many rows. How can you isolate the exact student matching a target numerical identifier and extract only their name and age columns?

hints.title: Boolean Indexing Invariant
hints.text: Filtering rows using a boolean comparison mask isolates records where the predicate holds true, followed by column subset projection.

hints.title: Mask and Projection Procedure
hints.text: Construct a boolean mask comparing student identifier column to one hundred and one. Index the DataFrame with the mask and project the name and age column list.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import pandas as pd

def selectData(students: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return students[students['student_id'] == 101][['name', 'age']]
```

complexity.notes: Vectorized boolean filtering and column subset projection.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row-by-row iteration with iterrows() incurs Python overhead and takes orders of magnitude longer than vectorized indexing.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boolean vector indexing creates a lightweight view or filtered copy in O(N) time with minimal auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Idiomatic boolean indexing and column projection in pandas; clean return DataFrame.
